DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 65 s. 2022 JUL 08 2022 HON. NHICOLLE B. CAPANGPANGAN President Sangguniang Kabataan Pederasyon Iligan City Dear SK President Capangpangan. This pertains to your letter dated 17 June 2022 requesting for a legal opinion on the propriety of the approved resolution by the Sangguniang Kabataan Pederasyon Officers of Iligan city declaring the SK Pederasyon Vice-President position as vacant. We find DILG Opinion No. 17, series of 2020, instructive as regards your query. Said Department opinion also dwelt on the query from the Pasig City Vice-Mayor on the legality of the resolution passed by the SK Federation of that local government unit declaring positions of the officers of the said federation vacant through a resolution, pertinent portions of which is hereunder provided, viz: "Our view is in the negative. We opine that said resolutions, in effect, removed all SK Federation Officers of Pasig City not in accordance to the governing rules on the matter. Section 21(c) or Republic Act No. 10742, otherwise known as the Sangguniang Kabataan Reform Act of 2015 is relevant. It states: SEC. 21. Pederasyon ng Sangguniang Kabataan. — (a) There shall be an organization of the Pederasyon ng mg Sangguniang Kabataan to be known as follows: xxx (c) The manner of election, suspension and removal of the officers of the Pederasyon at all levels and the term of office of the other officers of the Pederasyon shall be governed by the guidelines to be jointly issued by the DILG, the COMELEC and the Commission within sixty (60) days upon the effectivity of this Act. Accordingly, DILG-COMELEC-NYC issued Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2017-01 (JMC 2017-01), dated 23 June 2017, which sets the guidelines on the conduct of SK Federation election and rules governing terms of office, suspension and removal of all SK Federation officers. Sections 31(a), 32(a) and 35 thereof state: Page | 1 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

SECTION 31. GROUNDS FOR DISCIPLINARY ACTIONS (b) Any SK Pederasyon Officer may be disciplined, suspended, or removed from office, after due notice and hearing, on any of the following grounds: I. 2. 3. 4. 5. xxx Abuse of authority; Commission of any offense involving moral turpitude or an offense punishable by at least prision mayor (6 years and I day to 12 years) imprisonment; Failure to perform official duties and functions as Pederasyon Officer; Commission of any violations cited in the respective IRP of the concerned Pederasyon; and Such other grounds as may be provided under the Local Government Code of 1991, this JMC and all other applicable general and special laws. SECTION 32. FORM AND FILING OF COMPLAINTS. - A verified complaint against any Pederasyon Officer shall be initiated only by any officer or member of the concerned Pederasyon and shall be filed before the following: b. Office of the President, in the case of Panlalawigan, Panlungsod/Bayan Pederasyon Presidents who are ex-officio members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Panlungsod 9HUC, ICC, or Component City), and the Pederasyon President of Pateros, NCR, respectively; xxx SECTION 35. SUSPENSION AND REMOVAL FROM OFFICE. - Any elected SK Pederasyon officer at all levels, after due process, may be suspended for not more than six (6) months, or removed from the office of the concemed Pederasyon, by a majority vote of all the members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod/Bayan or Panlalawigan concerned, or by the higher authorities, on grounds stated in Section 31(a)(b) of this JMC. It is clear in the foregoing that for an SK PEderasyon Officer may be removed from office in two ways: (I) By filing a verified complaint before the Office of the President only by any officer or member of the SK Federation concerned stating any of the grounds mentioned in Section 31(a) of JMC 2017-01; and (2) By a majority vote of all members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod. There being no resort to any of the two, the positions held by the incumbent SK Federation President and the rest of the officers may not just be casually declared vacant through resolution of the SK Federation. Nowhere in the rules does it provide declaration of vacancy or removal of officers through a mere resolution. " Page 2 of S "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

As you have presented in your letter, the majority of the members of the Pederasyon ng Sangguniang Kabataan of Iligan City filed a petition/complaint before the Office of the SK Pederasyon President against the SK Vice- President due to negligence of duty and loss of confidence. This act of filing a complaint, however, by the majority members of the sanggunian before the Office of the Sangguniang Kabataan Pederasyon President is not in accordance with Section 32 of the DILG-COMELEC- NYC JMC 2017-01, wherein said provision stated that, viz: "SECTION 32. FORM AND FILING OF COMPLAINTS. - A verified complaint against any Pederasyon Officer shall be initiated only by any officer or member of the concerned Pederasyon and shall be filed before the following: a. b. c. Office of the President, in the case of the Panlalawigan, PanlungsodÆayan Pederasyon Presidents who are ex-officio members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Panlunqsod (HUC, ICC or Component City), and the Pederasyon President of Pateros, NCR, respectively; or Sangguniang Panlalawigan. in the case of the Pambayang Pederasyon President who is an ex-officio member of the Sangguniang Bayan (municipality), whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; or Sanggunian concerned, in the case of other officers of the concernedPederasyon, whose decision shall be final and executory Hence, the proper recourse, under the said DILG-COMELEC-NYC JMC 2017-01 is to file a verified complaint before the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Iligan City, pursuant to item (c) of Section 32 of the said JMC 2017-01 , considering that items (a) and (b) of the same section are inapplicable, because the one complained about is the SK Pederasyon Vice- President. While your citation of the provisions under the Local Government Code of 1991 is well noted as regards the Constitution and By-Laws of the Pederasyon ng mga Sangguniang Kabataan, it is also worthy to emphasize that there is already a more recent law specifically governing the Sangguniang Kabataan, which is Republic Act No. 10742 or the Sangguniang Kabataan Reform Act of 2015, particularly Section 21 of the same, hereunder quoted, viz: "SEC. 21. Pederasyon ng Sangguniang Kabataan. — (a) There shall be an organization of the Pederasyon ng mga Sangguniang Kabataan to be known as follows: xxx xxx (2) In cities, the Panlungsod na Pederasyon ng mga Sangguniang Kabataan which shall be composed of the Sangguniang Kabataan chairpersons of barangays in the city; and Page 3 of 5 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

xxx xxx (c) The manner of election, suspension and removal of the officers of the Pederasyon at all levels and the term of office of the other officers of the Pederasyon shall be governed by the guidelines to be jointly issued by the DILG, the COMELEC and the Commission within sixty (60) days upon the effectivity of this Act. " Said provision is further reiterated under Section 22 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the said law. Hence, the DILG-COMELEC-NYC JMC 2017-01, was issued to govern the manner of removal of the officers of the Pederasyon at all levels. Please also take into consideration that under Section 27 of the DILG-COMELEC- NYC JMC 2017-01, albeit the SK Pederasyon was granted the liberty to adopt its own internal rules of procedure, the same was not without limits, thus, the said provision was presented in this manner, viz: "SECTION 27. INTERNAL RULES OF PROCEDURE (IRP)- The Pederasyon ng mga Sangguniang Kabataan Officers at all levels shall formulate its IRP, and shall adhere to the following: a. b. I. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. Conduct the first regular session following the elections of the Pederasyon Officers and within ninety (90) days thereafter, the Pederasyon concerned shall formulate its IRP, The rules ofprocedure shall consist, but not limited to the following: Organization or creation of committees, such as committee on sports, advocacy, livelihood program, and other youth relat committees; Date, time and place ofsession or meeting; The order and calendar of business foreach session or meeting; Disciplinary actions or penalty for disordeny behavior and absences dunng session or meeting; Payment of pederasyon dues; and Such other rules as the Pederasyon may adopt, in accordance with existing laws, ordinances and govemment issuances. " It is on this regard that the Internal Rules of Procedure of the SK Pederasyon must always be in accordance with existing laws, ordinances, and government issuance. For one, the DILG-COMELEC-NYC JMC 2017-01, is a government issuance which specifically detailed how removal of a Pederasyon officer should be done. Secondly, a categorical definition of what a permanent vacancy and temporary vacancy are readily provided under Section 41 of the DILG-COMELEC-NYC JMC 2017-01. In parallel, the Local Government Code of 1991, particularly Sections 44 and 46, defines Permanent and Temporary vacancies. page 4 Of 5 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

It behooves upon this Department to lay down the premise on the established definition of permanent or temporary vacancy under our laws or existing rules because, internal rules of procedures are supposed to conform and follow settled laws/rules, in your case, the IRP of the SK Pederasyon of Iligan City, in essence, has provided another mode by which vacancy may exist. An act which is not supported under existing laws. As in fact, we are a government of law/rules and not of men, hence, as the old maxim goes, the spring cannot rise above its source, neither can an Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) of the SK Pederasyon be at variance with the statute and the constitution. Finally, your invocation of DILG Opinion No. 7, series of 2022, wherein the Pederasyons at all levels are mandated to formulate and adopt their respective IRPs, pursuant to Section 23 (2) of the 2017-01 JMC, which may provide, among others, rules and regulations internal to their organization, the same Opinion has invoked Section 23 (2) of the DILG- COMELEC-NYC JMC 2017-01 , that the IRPs that may be adopted by the pederasyon must not be contrary to existing laws, ordinances, and other governmental issuances. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion that will be rendered by more competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Underse ry for Local Governmen OUSLG/MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/rrao/clp copy furnish: DIR. ANEL M. AGABE Regional Director, DILG Region X KM3 Fr. W.F.
